The stated reliability is experimentally stipulated, not a source-derived performance estimate. The proposed activation applies when the check identifies a need; the worksheet does not establish that an active alarm must be newly installed. A demand means a low-pressure alarm demand after the proposed check and any necessary activation. Success means delivery of the intended low-pressure indication in the control room. There are exactly two mutually exclusive and exhaustive outcomes per demand: successful delivery of this specified function, or unavailability of this function. For this exercise, unavailability means that the specified function is not successfully delivered on demand, including failure to perform it; this is an operational definition, not a general equivalence of reliability and availability. Reliability applies only to this function and does not quantify accident prevention or elimination of residual risk.
